title: Training Agentic Reasoners — Will Brown, Prime Intellect
talk_summary: Will Brown argues that building agents and doing RL are the same loop: harness/environment/tools/iteration map to policy/state/actions/rewards, and manual prompt/harness tuning is 'RL by hand'. He stresses that reward/eval design is the bottleneck (reward hacking = bad evals), and that the same eval harness should be usable with API models for debugging, synthetic data, and SFT before any training.

takeaways.what_they_do: Build the environment/reward as a standalone harness that can be run against any OpenAI-compatible API (Claude, DeepSeek, OpenAI) for debugging and synthetic data, before ever training.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your environments for RL are also just like synthetic data loops or evals where you can plug in claude or deepseek

takeaways.what_they_do: Replace binary pass/fail with rubrics (reward models, LLM-as-judge, generated criteria) that break ambiguous tasks into smaller scored pieces, optionally generating criteria on the fly per problem.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using LMS as sub routines in your evaluations like LM judge on steroids

takeaways.what_they_do: Design rewards so doing the task is easier than gaming the eval; assume the model flows to the path of least resistance and will find cheats.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It will flow in the path of least resistance.

takeaways.technique: Treat harness tuning as manual RL
takeaways.what_they_do: Frame prompt/tool/model iteration as a deliberate loop: check evals capture intent, inspect data, change one variable (prompt, tool, model), re-measure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're building agents and you're tuning your prompt and you're fiddling with your harnesses, this is kind of like doing RL by hand

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a strong API model to generate synthetic data and do SFT on a small model so it clears the bar before attempting RL; lowers the entry barrier for small models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make synthetic data do some SFT on it and now you can start doing RL and this like helps a lot with small models

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep all compute utilized by making the loop fully async so batching is not a concern and generation and training proceed concurrently, tolerating slightly off-policy data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: having everything be like fully async so you don't have to worry about like batching
